in_latin.name: Wiborada
in_latin.long_meaning: Wiborada, a female given name, is derived from Germanic 'Wibi' and 'Rada', indicating friendship or advice. In Christian tradition, the name is associated with Saint Wiborada, a 9th-century martyr and abbess of a convent in St. Gall, Switzerland. Her feast day is celebrated on February 2. The name is thought to have been introduced to Britain by the Normans and has since been adopted in various forms, including Wiborad and Wiborade. In modern times, the name Wiborada is occasionally used in Christian cultures to reflect the values of friendship, loyalty, and spiritual guidance.
